target_customer: Nigerian and wider African retail investors, and wealthy individuals via asset managers, who want US and local stocks
problem: Africans had little access to US securities, and buying one required an asset manager calling an international broker.
business_model: Brokerage commissions and fees on trades and products, via a partner broker dealer

founders.name: Richmond Bassey
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Jan 2022 names him as founder. Background not found.

founders.name: Yanmo Omorogbe
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and as COO by TechCrunch. Background not found.

competitors.name: Chaka
competitors.what: Nigerian app for local and foreign stocks and ETFs

competitors.name: Trove
competitors.what: Micro investing app for Nigerian and foreign stocks

technical_complexity.rationale: A trading app on a partner broker (DriveWealth) is standard, but cross border funding, FX and Nigerian regulation are hard.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses from Nigeria's SEC and a US broker dealer affiliate took years, while rivals used the same partners.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. A rival, Risevest, acquired Chaka.

market_need_then: TechCrunch says 75 percent of users had never traded before and 50,000 joined the Ghana waitlist. In 2020, Nigerians sought dollar assets, though that point is the company's pitch rather than a sourced spend figure.

branding.domain_note: Uses investbamboo.com, suggesting bamboo.com was unavailable; not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational, with the tagline Dream, Invest, Live

branding.community_and_virality: Over 50,000 people joined the waitlist for the Ghana launch, per TechCrunch Jan 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: Ranked first by downloads among Nigerian stock apps in an Aug 2025 Nairametrics list per search results, and covered by TechCrunch. No evidence of mascot or merch.

outcome_analysis: Bamboo launched in January 2020, reached over 300,000 users by early 2022 and raised a $15M Series A co-led by Greycroft and Tiger Global in January 2022. It later gained a Nigerian sub broker licence, a US broker dealer affiliate in 2024, expanded to South Africa and added Nigerian stocks and a remittance app. It claims 2.3M users. A 2021 SEC circular shows regulatory risk that it navigated.
notes: The $2.4M earlier raise is stated by TechCrunch without date or investors; stage unstated so other. Series A also reported by TechCabal and others. Aggregators gave total funding of $17.5M and $19.4M, unverified. Competitors are from a 2020 Condia comparison seen in search results and a Jan 2022 TechCrunch article. The user count of 2.3M is a company claim. Name origin not found.
